overall_summary: Recent 7-day performance data clearly demonstrates that space-themed 'What If' scenarios and extreme planetary facts (e.g., liquid diamond planets, burning ice planets, dark planets) generate the highest views-per-day, likes-per-view, and engagement. Videos framing hypothetical catastrophic or bizarre planetary conditions (e.g., IYuce8vaU3Y, 8KEl0_pJ_68, 6pwazIPnOHw) dramatically outperform standard declarative facts or older psychology/history shorts. The audience responds best to second-person immersive framing ('What If You Fell Into...') combined with extreme, counter-intuitive visual phenomena.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) pulled 1,024 views with 38 likes quickly, and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) reached 972 views.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form speculative physics and extreme space scenarios focusing on bizarre alien worlds using second-person perspective.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (QXuqYERlqSo) consistently achieve high views and strong like ratios relative to older content.
winning_patterns.action: Continue focusing on exotic exoplanets with extreme weather or bizarre material properties, pairing them with striking visual hooks.

weak_patterns.evidence: Shorts like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A) and 'The 2,000-Year-Old Mystery' (yLm-FjYH6-k) stagnated with very low view counts (<150 views) and zero comments.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract human psychology and static historical mysteries unless they feature an immediate, visceral physical hook or shocking experiment.

weak_patterns.pattern: Declarative Space Facts Without Immersive Framing
weak_patterns.evidence: Simple declarative titles like 'This Star Is Older Than the Universe!' (vFXHTmYITp4) stalled at 11 views, whereas framing them as scenarios or active questions drives traffic.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid plain statement titles; always frame space facts as high-stakes questions or 'What If' exploratory hooks.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Coldest Known Planet (OGLE-TR-56b or WD 1856+534 style rogue dead star system)? Let's explore absolute zero atmospheric freezing instantly turning human tissue to brittle glass.
next_video.opening_direction: Start mid-fall through an invisible, pitch-black atmosphere where your breath freezes before it leaves your lungs.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that you aren't falling toward a solid surface, but rather descending endlessly into a crushing, hyper-dense core of exotic degenerate matter.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high-performing 'What If You Fell Into...' space format which shows superior velocity in views and like-to-view conversion.
fresh_topic_constraints: Do not use diamonds, glass rain, rubies, or burning ice.
Do not reuse any previously covered exoplanets or stars.
Focus strictly on absolute zero physics and extreme cold mechanics.

experiment: Test a 21-second 'What If' space scenario with an accelerated audio intro (under 1.5 seconds to first visual transition) to measure retention lift compared to baseline pacing.
